### DEBT [consistency]: src/domains/verify/verify.ts:351
Reference: spx/34-verification.enabler/32-verify.enabler/65-review.enabler/15-review-payload.pdr.md product property 1-2: "A review envelope records provider identity when present, actor, state, body, submitted time, commit identity, and URL when present" / "A review comment records provider identity when present, path, line or position, side, ... URL when present ...".
Evidence: readOptionalString (verify.ts:351-357) is byte-for-byte identical to readRequiredString (verify.ts:343-349) - both just return undefined when the value is not a non-empty string. validateReviewFinding, validateReviewScope, and validateReviewTerminalMetadata all read providerIdentity/url through readOptionalString, so there is no way to distinguish field-absent from field-present-with-wrong-type. A payload such as providerIdentity: 123, url: 456 is accepted by all three validators, with providerIdentity/url silently coerced to absent rather than the payload being rejected - the same silent-drop applies to line/position via readOptionalPositiveInteger for a non-integer or non-positive value. This lets a producer bug, such as sending a numeric id where a string was expected, pass validation undetected instead of failing loud at the evidence boundary the PDR describes.
Required: give the optional-field readers a distinct present-but-invalid outcome, e.g. a tri-state or a validation error, so validateReviewFinding, validateReviewScope, and validateReviewTerminalMetadata reject a payload whose optional field is present with the wrong type instead of silently treating it as omitted.

### DEBT [evidence]: testing/generators/verify/verify.ts (arbitraryReviewScopeUnit)
Reference: spx/34-verification.enabler/32-verify.enabler/65-review.enabler/15-review-payload.pdr.md product property 3: "a reviewed scope unit records provider identity when present, path, optional line or position range, side, commit identity, coverage state, and optional URL"; and 21-review-evidence-model.enabler/review-evidence-model.md conformance assertion with the same schema description.
Evidence: this PR new validateReviewScope in src/domains/verify/verify.ts accepts a scope unit with position instead of line, with neither line nor position, and with optional providerIdentity/url. But arbitraryReviewScopeUnit in testing/generators/verify/verify.ts always sets a fixed line and never sets position, never omits both, and never sets providerIdentity/url - so VERIFY_TEST_GENERATOR.reviewScopeUnit and scopePayload, and the harness assertions built on them, assertValidReviewScopeRecordsScopeEvidenceKind and assertAppendPayloadChannelDoesNotReuseRunInput in testing/harnesses/verify/harness.ts, only ever exercise one of the several shapes the new validator accepts. Separately, assertAppendPayloadChannelDoesNotReuseRunInput loops over Object.values of the scope payload and calls expect(recordedEvent).toContain(value) for each - this now includes the numeric line field, and it only keeps passing because toContain on a string coerces the number via ToString, so the assertion for line is coincidental: it would likely still pass by matching a stray digit inside the 40-character hex commit field even if line were dropped from the recorded event, rather than being a reliable regression check.
Required: extend arbitraryReviewScopeUnit to cover position-only, neither-anchor, and providerIdentity/url-present shapes, mirroring how arbitraryReviewFinding already covers line-only, position-only, and both; and replace the numeric-field toContain check with a typed equality assertion on the recorded event data.
